title: The address that hands Play Console each release bundle has no test at all
what: Play Console pulls each new release bundle and its store pictures through our own address. No test asks it for a bundle, a missing version, a picture, a wrong method or the browser first-ask, so a break would only show on release day.
expected: A small test asks the address for a bundle, a missing one, a picture, a POST and an OPTIONS ask, and checks the answer, the size, no caching and the Play-only browser rule.
fix_line: Add a test for the release bundle address with a fake GitHub

title: The download link for phones without Google Play has no test
what: The link that gives the newest MettleUp app file to a phone without Google Play is never asked for in a test: not the newest file, not the fallback page when GitHub cannot be reached, not the 10-minute wait after a release.
expected: A test asks the link with a fake GitHub and checks it points at the newest file, falls back to the release page, and keeps the answer for no more than 10 minutes.
fix_line: Add a test for the phone app download link

title: The public page a check-in poster opens is never tested
what: Scanning the check-in poster without the app opens a public page. No test opens it on Android, on an iPhone, with an old poster, or when the gym server is down, so none of its words or its no-check-in-from-home rule is checked.
expected: A screen test opens the poster page for each of those cases and checks the words and that nothing is recorded by the page.
fix_line: Add a screen test for the check-in poster page

title: The limit of 30 friend enquiries a day for one gym is never tested
what: The friend page has three daily limits. Two are tested (one address, one link). The third, 30 a day for one whole gym, is never reached in any test.
expected: The friend database test fills a gym with 30 friend enquiries and checks the next one is refused with nothing half-made.
fix_line: Add the 30-a-day gym check to the friend database test

title: Nothing checks a new gym name or logo reaches the invite link within 5 minutes
what: The invite link page keeps each gym's name and logo for 5 minutes. No test checks that time, so a change could stick for much longer without anyone noticing.
expected: A test checks the kept copy lasts 5 minutes and that a changed name and logo show after it.
how_often: after a name or logo change
fix_line: Test the 5-minute keep time of the invite preview

title: What's new: the keep times, the 5-line limit and the broken-file rule are never tested
what: The What's new feed keeps a fresh copy 10 minutes and a last good copy a week, shows at most 5 lines, and must never keep or pass on a broken file. None of these is tested; only the two ways to GitHub and the 503 are.
expected: Tests check 6 lines become 5, a broken file is not kept, and the 10-minute and one-week times.
fix_line: Add the keep-time and broken-file cases to the What's new test

title: The one-year delete of feedback messages is never tested
what: The privacy notice promises feedback is deleted after a year. The run that deletes it, and the run that sorts messages, have no test, so nothing proves old messages really go.
expected: A test puts in a message older than a year and one newer, runs the delete, and checks only the old one is gone.
fix_line: Add a test for the feedback delete and sort runs

title: The invite and get-app pages' own words are mostly never checked
what: Tests check which part of each page shows, but not most of its words: the WhatsApp preview 'Join <gym> on MettleUp', 'First, get the MettleUp app' with its steps, 'Get it on Google Play', the code box, 'Open this link on your phone', and the iPhone and computer headlines of the get-app page.
expected: The screen tests assert these words for each kind of phone and the preview title set by the server.
fix_line: Add the missing words to the link page screen tests

title: Admin app feedback: the journey expects the gym code, the test says none is sent
what: The journey says the owner's and desk's feedback is kept with the gym code. The admin app's test checks the opposite: the message carries nothing about the gym.
expected: The map and the code agree: either the journey drops the gym code, or the admin app sends it and the test checks it.
fix_line: Decide whether admin feedback carries the gym code and fix the journey or the test

title: A retry after a failed save, and the daily feedback limit lifting, are never tested
what: No test saves a message after a failed try and checks there is one copy and the failure did not count, and no test checks the 20-a-day limit lifts after 24 hours.
expected: Tests send after a failure and after the 24 hours pass, and check one copy and a working send.
fix_line: Add the retry and next-day cases to the feedback test
